newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER ON CENTRAL BANK DEFENCE.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER ON CENTRAL BANK DEFENCE.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday due to suspected central bank intervention to defend the local unit, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$28.725, after trading at a narrow T$28.718-727 range, against Wednesday's T$28.727 close.
Turnover through dealers was active at US$237 million.
"Like yesterday, the central bank tried to sell U.S. dollars to prevent the Taiwan dollar from falling below T$28.727," said one dealer.
"It seems meaningless to defend the T$28.727 level, but maybe the central bank tried to warn speculators that recent Taiwan dollar depreciation has almost come to an end," the dealer said.
He said the Taiwan dollar may turn to test its upside on Friday, seeing a range of T$28.68-73.
